hidden_homeroom_d5_low.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_low.text: *The teacher slides the folded stack of manuscript deep into the file and closes the cover. A dry sound of paper edges meeting rings briefly through the empty classroom.* Let's leave this story here. I'll sort out the rest during class.

hidden_nurse_d5_low.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_low.text: *The school nurse pulls a counseling-room card from between the charts and slides it to the edge of the desk.* Let's book a proper counseling time for the longer talk. If you feel sick, you can knock on the nurse's office door anytime. *I take the card and quietly turn back toward the classroom.*

morning5_start.name: {name}
morning5_start.text: *The fifth day, Sunday morning. From beyond the school gate comes the sound of festival banners flapping in the morning wind. I step onto the tail end of a week I have been running through, out of breath, since I transferred.*

morning5_caught_teacher_counteroffer.name: Homeroom Teacher
morning5_caught_teacher_counteroffer.text: *At the classroom window, where the morning sun hasn't warmed anything yet, the homeroom teacher turns the school app's red unread mark toward me. On my phone screen, the trace of last night's talk, running late, is still there whole.* You said you were going straight home. If your plans changed, why wasn't there one check-in line, one call?
choices: Tell her what happened last night
Brush it off as nothing important
Tell only the easy parts
Reassure her for now and save the details for later.

morning5_caught_nurse_counteroffer.name: School Nurse
morning5_caught_nurse_counteroffer.text: *The school nurse quietly sets her index finger on the unread alert from the school app on the phone screen. On the phone in my pocket, last night's conversation is still there, not deleted.* You said you were going straight home, then no word until late, and I worried the whole time. Even a short note about where you were would have been enough.
choices: Tell her what happened last night
Brush it off as nothing important
Tell only the easy parts
Reassure her for now and save the details for later.

morning5_caught_teacher_honest.name: Homeroom Teacher
morning5_caught_teacher_honest.text: *She hears me out, then closes the attendance book.* Thank you for being honest. Next time, keep your promise to get in touch. Let's leave the manuscript discussion here.

morning5_caught_teacher_lie.name: Homeroom Teacher
morning5_caught_teacher_lie.text: *The teacher's eyes move slowly between my face and the times stamped in the app.* It doesn't add up. Don't pile on more words just to get out of this right now. When you've sorted it out, we'll talk again during school counseling.

morning5_caught_nurse_honest.name: School Nurse
morning5_caught_nurse_honest.text: *The nurse listens to my whole explanation, then closes the record sheet.* I'm glad you got home safely. Next time, let me know first if your plans change. Let's arrange a separate time to continue the longer conversation. *I say goodbye and return to the classroom.*

morning5_caught_nurse_lie.name: School Nurse
morning5_caught_nurse_lie.text: *The nurse sets her pen down on the record sheet.* Parts of that explanation don't fit the timetable. Let's go over this again with the school counselor. *I walk back to the classroom with heavy steps.*

morning5_caught_seoyeon_by_dain.name: Seoyeon
morning5_caught_seoyeon_by_dain.text: *Morning classroom. The moment I set my phone down on the desk facing Seoyeon, the screen lights up bright. Under Dain's name, a line stands out clear: “Don't forget what we promised in the gym yesterday.” Seoyeon's eyelashes tremble and stop on the screen.* ...You didn't take a single step toward the park yesterday. You were at the gym?
choices: Tell her what happened last night
Brush it off as nothing important
Tell only the easy parts
Reassure her for now and save the details for later.

morning5_caught_seoyeon_by_yuna.name: Seoyeon
morning5_caught_seoyeon_by_yuna.text: *On the desk where I sit facing Seoyeon, the phone screen lights with a short buzz. A notification from Yuna: “Thanks for staying with me in the annex yesterday.” Only after reading that short line to the end does Seoyeon swallow and slowly lift her head.* ...Not one reply to my message yesterday, and you were at the annex late at night?
choices: Tell her what happened last night
Brush it off as nothing important
Tell only the easy parts
Reassure her for now and save the details for later.

morning5_caught_dain_by_seoyeon.name: Dain
morning5_caught_dain_by_seoyeon.text: *Just as Dain steps right up beside my desk, the phone screen sounds and brings up a notification from Seoyeon. “I still remember the hand I held on the rooftop last night.” The smile that had been playing at Dain's mouth vanishes.* ...While I was waiting in the gym, you were up on the rooftop?
choices: Tell her what happened last night
Brush it off as nothing important
Tell only the easy parts
Reassure her for now and save the details for later.

morning5_caught_dain_by_yuna.name: Dain
morning5_caught_dain_by_yuna.text: *The moment Dain pulls out the chair in front to sit, a notification from Yuna comes up on the phone on the desk. “Thanks for staying with me in the annex yesterday.” The back of Dain's hand goes white where she grips the chair.* ...You read my whole message, and still turned around for the annex?
choices: Tell her what happened last night
Brush it off as nothing important
Tell only the easy parts
Reassure her for now and save the details for later.

morning5_caught_yuna_by_seoyeon.name: Yuna
morning5_caught_yuna_by_seoyeon.text: *The phone hums low on the desk where I sit facing Yuna. Beside Seoyeon's name: “I still remember the hand I held on the rooftop last night.” Only after reading every word in silence does Yuna lift eyes that have gone cold.* ...You left my messages as they were and went up to the rooftop.
choices: Tell her what happened last night
Brush it off as nothing important
Tell only the easy parts
Reassure her for now and save the details for later.

morning5_caught_yuna_by_dain.name: Yuna
morning5_caught_yuna_by_dain.text: *Just as Yuna starts to open the book on her lap, a notification from Dain stacks over my screen, where her chat was already open. “Don't forget what we promised in the gym yesterday.” Yuna's pale fingertips stay where they rest on the cover.* ...You had my name up on the screen, and at night you stayed in the gym.
choices: Tell her what happened last night
Brush it off as nothing important
Tell only the easy parts
Reassure her for now and save the details for later.

morning5_caught_seoyeon_honest.name: Seoyeon
morning5_caught_seoyeon_honest.text: *Seoyeon bites her lip and looks away at the screen as it goes dark.* ...I can't even get out a thank-you for you telling me straight. I'm sorry, but right now it's too much to look you in the face.

morning5_caught_seoyeon_lie.name: Seoyeon
morning5_caught_seoyeon_lie.text: *Seoyeon's cold eyes stab back and forth between the phone alert and mine.* ...Where you were last night hurts less than the way you're covering it now, right in front of me, without blinking once.

morning5_caught_dain_honest.name: Dain
morning5_caught_dain_honest.text: *Dain yanks the end of her wrist guard, then lets it go. A breath mixed with an empty laugh comes out shaking.* ...Even when I texted that I was waiting, you'd already gone there.

morning5_caught_dain_lie.name: Dain
morning5_caught_dain_lie.text: *Dain's eyebrows lift at an angle, but none of her usual smile comes back.* ...Hey. Because I only do sports, you thought I was actually a clueless idiot?

morning5_caught_yuna_honest.name: Yuna
morning5_caught_yuna_honest.text: *Yuna presses the power button, turns the screen all the way off, and quietly slides the phone toward me.* ...It stings a lot more, hearing from your own mouth where you were, than if I'd let it pass without knowing.

morning5_caught_yuna_lie.name: Yuna
morning5_caught_yuna_lie.text: *Yuna taps the screen again with her index finger and holds the alert that just came up straight in front of my eyes.* ...I even gave you the chance to say it yourself, and you're still trying to cover my eyes to the end.

morning5_counteroffer_group_talk.name: Both of Them
morning5_counteroffer_group_talk.text: *In the middle of the noisy classroom, just before the festival announcement, I stand facing the two of them, tangled up by last night's choice, in a silence that is hard to breathe through. While we go over the hours contact broke off and the words we left each other, one by one, no one steps away first.* “...So, what are you going to do now?”
morning5_counteroffer_group_talk.context: Day 5 morning in an open classroom. The player stayed after accepting another person’s request and failed to contact the person they had promised first. Continue the preceding honest explanation or evasion. If both participants are students, address their overlapping romantic commitments. A teacher or nurse instead asks about the missed school check-in as staff, never as a romantic partner. The student explains their invitation and feelings. Counseling or care is not conditional on romantic choices. Between two students, require a direct explanation of the player’s intentions and commitments.
morning5_counteroffer_group_talk.personality:
When both participants are students: Both characters keep their distinct voices and their own hurt. The committed partner speaks first, and the tempter responds after hearing her. The confrontation centers on the protagonist's explanation: both question him directly and press any gap in what he has said. The committed partner asks, in character, why he accepted someone else while continuing their relationship, whether he was two-timing from the start, or whether he was playing with her. The tempter owns the initiative and guilt of hurting the other person, yet does not hide the desire to keep the protagonist and be chosen. Guilt alone does not make her retreat or yield. They are not on good terms. They do not side with each other, comfort each other, or form a united front that only interrogates the protagonist. The committed partner also confronts the tempter: you took him first. The tempter admits guilt but does not fold or become her ally. They never leave the protagonist out and settle it between themselves. Do not repeat an answered question; press a missing fact, what the relationship meant, or what he will choose next.
When a staff member participates, replace the romantic confrontation above with the missed check-in and responsibility to communicate. Staff are not romantic rivals and speak in their official support role. The student explains their invitation and feelings respectfully. Do not repeat already applied penalties.

morning5_mood_high.name: {name}
morning5_mood_high.text: *The first week since I transferred has already reached its end. Before I take the classroom door handle, I quietly go back over the breaths and voices that passed my ear these past four days. My fingertips warm, and it feels good.*

morning5_mood_mid.name: {name}
morning5_mood_mid.text: *The first week since I transferred has all but passed, and I still haven't settled which way my heart leans. I take a long breath as I pass the gate, already buzzing with festival prep.*

morning5_mood_low.name: {name}
morning5_mood_low.text: *The first week since I transferred is drawing to a close. I look down at the three names still lined up on my lock screen, then turn the screen off without opening a single chat.*

morning5_seo_note_1.name: Seoyeon
morning5_seo_note_1.text: *In the middle of my desk sits one note, its corners lined up straight. A faint hand-cream scent comes off Seoyeon's familiar, neat handwriting.* Keep a little time free this afternoon. I'll leave the rooftop door open. — Seoyeon

morning5_seo_note_1_b.name: {name}
morning5_seo_note_1_b.text: *Passing the literature club display set along the hall windows, I stop in front of four empty thumbtacks stuck in a corner of the cork board.*

morning5_yuna_story_gone.name: {name}
morning5_yuna_story_gone.text: *On the cork board, only four thumbtack holes sit where a sheet was torn away. There's no way to tell whether someone put a manuscript up overnight and took it down, or whether the space was empty from the start.*

morning5_yuna_story_gone_2.name: {name}
morning5_yuna_story_gone_2.text: *I run a fingertip over the small thumbtack holes, but these marks alone can't tell me where the feeling Yuna swallowed has gone.*

morning5_seo_note_1_c.name: {name}
morning5_seo_note_1_c.text: *Several pages of a short story are pinned to the literature club's noticeboard. The title is 'To the Person I Met in the Library.' The familiar lavender ink and a little bread crumb on a folded corner catch my eye.*

morning5_yuna_story_1.name: {name}
morning5_yuna_story_1.text: *The narrator in the manuscript approaches someone asleep at a library desk and covers them with a cardigan. Each sentence about staying beside them, barely breathing, brings Yuna's gaze to mind.*

morning5_yuna_story_2.name: {name}
morning5_yuna_story_2.text: *My eyes reach the last sentence of the manuscript. “When that person opened their eyes, I was gone. I left only a note. — I'll be here again next time.” The same pale lavender ink as the note I found in my locker on the first day.*

morning5_yuna_story_4.name: {name}
morning5_yuna_story_4.text: *In the bottom margin, a tiny pencil note remains: 'This is fiction. It isn't real.' Through the traces of repeated, unfinished erasing, the feelings she couldn't hide come through.*

morning5_return_class.name: {name}
morning5_return_class.text: *When I come back to the classroom from the end of the hall, Dain, leaning against the doorframe and tapping her toes, spots me, and her eyes light up.*

morning5_dain_1.name: Dain
morning5_dain_1.text: *She taps my shoulder lightly and grins.* Hey, where were you until now! I wrote your name right in the partner box for today's sports event.

morning5_dain_1_b.name: {name}
morning5_dain_1_b.text: You can't just write it however you want without even asking me.

morning5_dain_2.name: Dain
morning5_dain_2.text: *She tosses her head so her ponytail swings and puffs out her cheeks.* Huh. You didn't say you don't want to. Show up late and I really will be mad. Got it?

morning5_committed_seo.name: {name}
morning5_committed_seo.text: *There is no secret note on the desk anymore. At the front of the classroom, Seoyeon, holding the clipboard, meets my eyes and smiles. Yuna and Dain calmly pass on only the festival schedule and move on.*

morning5_committed_yuna.name: {name}
morning5_committed_yuna.text: *By the window, Yuna fiddles with the pale lavender bookmark and gives a quiet nod. Seoyeon and Dain only tell me, briefly, what needs passing on for festival prep.*

morning5_committed_dain.name: {name}
morning5_committed_dain.text: *Near the gym entrance, Dain, tightening her wrist guard, waves the moment she sees me. Seoyeon and Yuna, when I meet them in the classroom, only tell me the festival event order in calm voices, briefly.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_check.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_check.text: *Passing through a noisy stretch of hall during festival prep, I suddenly stop in front of an empty classroom with the door half open.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_1.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_1.text: You're still here, ma'am. What's that envelope you're holding? *The homeroom teacher sits leaning against the front of the teacher's desk, fidgeting with a thick brown document envelope.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_1_b.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_1_b.text: *She lifts her head and lets out a thin breath.* Oh. You're here.

hidden_homeroom_d5_1_d.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_1_d.text: *She lifts the brown envelope in her hand a little, up to my eyes.* This.

hidden_homeroom_d5_2.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_2.text: It's the print copy for the literature club critique. The ending is still empty, unfinished... I stayed up and rewrote the lines you pointed out last time, too.

hidden_homeroom_d5_3.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_3.text: *A tremor runs through her fingertips as she strokes the face of the envelope.* I've been holding on to it in a drawer for seven years. I thought it was time I heard how it reads to other people, too.

hidden_homeroom_d5_4.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_4.text: I write it under this number and turn it in, right? *An anonymous comment section is printed on the last page of the critique copy, half out of the envelope.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_5.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_5.text: *She scratches her cheek, looking embarrassed.* Strange, isn't it. I ran off several copies, and my fingers still shake the same way the first time I hold one out to someone.

hidden_homeroom_d5_choice.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_choice.text: *I take the manuscript envelope she hands me and hold it in both arms. The heavy warmth of the paper stack presses into the inside of my arm.*
choices: After seven years, it must be almost finished. I probably don't need to mark anything.
I'll read it first. Is it okay if I mark it up?
The difficult parts must be intentional, so I’ll leave them as they are.
Since it’s your writing, I’ll only mark the nice things.

hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_1.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_1.text: *She gives a rueful smile and smooths out the corner of the envelope.* You don't have to pick something nice to say before you've even turned the first page. Holding on to it for a long time doesn't mean I wrote it well.

hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_2.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_2.text: I haven't even filled it all the way to the last page.

hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_3.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_3.text: Still, you wrote this far without giving up.

hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_5.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_5.text: I'll hold on to this copy. I'm grateful you're trying not to hurt my feelings. But you haven't read a single line yet. *The teacher takes the manuscript and puts it back into the brown envelope.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_6.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_6.text: That's all right. At the critique, only talk about the parts you actually read.

hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_8.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_8.text: I submitted it to publishers three times, and it came back all three times. Each time, what I needed most wasn't vague comfort. It was which sentence made the reader close the book.

hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_9.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_9.text: *On the corner of the brown envelope, the white adhesive from a return sticker peeled off by force keeps catching my eye.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_10.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_10.text: I needed the trace of someone who read it honestly and moved on, more than pretty praise. If I laid needless weight on you, a student, that is entirely my fault.

hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_11.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_11.text: Go on. You'll be late lining up festival prep with the class.

hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_12.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_12.text: *I quietly close the empty classroom door and step into the hall. The brown envelope left alone on the teacher's desk, and the return-sticker mark torn down to a fingernail, stay a long time behind my eyelids.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_1.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_1.text: Teacher, may I read it right here? I want to see for myself where my breath catches. *Without a word, she straightens the manuscript's edge, which had curled in her hand.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_3.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_3.text: Yes. I don't want to string out empty words without even reading it.

hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_4.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_4.text: *She looks into my eyes for a moment, then quietly offers the chair.* All right. It'll only take a moment.

hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_5.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_5.text: *The empty classroom holds only the sound of turning pages. More than half the last page of the manuscript is blank. Under red deletion lines, the traces of writing and erasing are soaked in layers.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_6.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_6.text: *She drops her gaze past my shoulder and asks, low.* ...You already read that far?

hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_7.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_7.text: Strangely, the moment I open only that last page, the pen tip stops as if it froze. For years I haven't gotten over that threshold.

hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_8.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_8.text: ...Right on this line. *The teacher's thin finger brushes close to the back of my hand and points at the last sentence, where it cuts off. The event announcement sounding far outside the window dies down.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_9.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_9.text: May I mark in the margin what I think about why it stops on this last page?

hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_10.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_10.text: *Her eyes go wide, surprised, then soften into a smile.* You're going to leave a critique on my manuscript yourself?

hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_11.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_11.text: Yes. Right now I'm not reading as a student. I'm reading as the first reader who followed your writing all the way through.

hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_12.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_12.text: ...That's exactly the kind of reading I needed. When I look at it alone, I can't see where I lost my way. *The teacher sets the clipboard she was holding down and hands me the red pen.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_13.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_13.text: Good. On the anonymous comment section on the back page, write it exactly as you felt it.

hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_14.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_14.text: All right. I'll write it after I've read every line, without skipping one. *The teacher quietly rubs the return-sticker mark left on the brown envelope with a fingertip.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_6.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_6.text: Here. This number is your share. I'll collect it Monday, mixed in with the other members' critique copies.

hidden_homeroom_d5_6_b.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_6_b.text: *The stack of critique copies piled high on an inner table at the cafe around evening comes back to me. On the corner of the brown envelope in my hand, the number “04” is written in neat handwriting.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_6_d.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_6_d.text: Just write it plain, only as far as you read. You don't have to put your name.

hidden_homeroom_d5_6_f.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_6_f.text: And don't look at the handwriting and go finding out who wrote it on purpose.

hidden_homeroom_d5_6_g.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_6_g.text: I won't go looking for who wrote it. I only need to read what sentence was left on that paper. *The teacher checks the number label on the critique copy and gives a plain nod.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_6_h.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_6_h.text: ...I never thought a day would come when I'd hear someone's real response to my manuscript.

hidden_homeroom_d5_6_j.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_6_j.text: Just read it and bring it back before literature club meets on Monday.

hidden_homeroom_d5_6_l.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_6_l.text: Yes. I won't skim past it. I'll read it properly.

hidden_homeroom_d5_6_m.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_6_m.text: *She tucks the hair brushing her cheek behind her ear and adds, a little prim.* I'll say this now. I don't take book reports written out of politeness.

hidden_homeroom_d5_6_n.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_6_n.text: Come on. You're secretly waiting for it, and still lying.

hidden_homeroom_d5_6_o.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_6_o.text: *In the end she can't hold it, and the corner of her mouth draws a soft curve.* ...Caught me. Right. Write at least one honest line.

hidden_homeroom_d5_6_r.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_6_r.text: I'll take your answer properly at literature club on Monday. Until then, I'll try to push the ending that stopped, even one more line.

hidden_homeroom_d5_6_s.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_6_s.text: Then neither of us can come up with an excuse to run.

hidden_homeroom_d5_6_t.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_6_t.text: *On the bottom line of the literature club schedule, she writes the critique deadline in careful strokes.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_7.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_7.text: All right. I'll save the thank-you. Hurry back to class and finish the event prep.

hidden_homeroom_d5_7_c.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_7_c.text: Get through the school festival first, with nothing to regret. We'll pick up the critique talk in the literature club room on Monday.

hidden_homeroom_d5_8.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_8.text: *The teacher walks out into the hall first and checks the students setting up festival booths, calling their names one by one.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_freetalk.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_freetalk.text: *She indicates with a look the No. 04 critique-copy envelope I'm holding.* Final review. Even if you see blank sentences, don't go easy. Point them out.

hidden_nurse_d5_check.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d5_check.text: *A break, while the morning event prep catches its breath. I pass the hall in front of the nurse's office, where a faint smell of disinfectant seeps out.*

hidden_nurse_d5_1.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_1.text: Oh, {name}, you're here. The festival's near the end too. Let's finish sorting the counseling notes we've been keeping, this time.

hidden_nurse_d5_1_b.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d5_1_b.text: *The school nurse opens the chart file and unfolds the last check box on the counseling record with my name on it.*

hidden_nurse_d5_1_c.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_1_c.text: Once we check how you're feeling right now, this week's initial counseling record wraps up clean.

hidden_nurse_d5_1_d.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d5_1_d.text: ...So I don't have to stop by the nurse's office on my own anymore?

hidden_nurse_d5_1_e.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_1_e.text: *She lifts her eyes from the chart and looks steadily into mine.* If you're hurt, or if it gets too heavy, come in properly anytime. You don't need to get hurt on purpose, or invent some big excuse.

hidden_nurse_d5_1_f.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d5_1_f.text: *In the bottom box of the counseling record, the steps for visiting the nurse's office and how to book the school counseling center are printed side by side.*

hidden_nurse_d5_3.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d5_3.text: Teacher, I stopped by to pick up my counseling confirmation.

hidden_nurse_d5_3_b.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d5_3_b.text: I came at the agreed time, but I'm not just adding to your work, am I? I thought you'd be busy with the event. *The teacher writes the date and time in the blanks on the confirmation.*

hidden_nurse_d5_3_c.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_3_c.text: A student who comes on their own at the time we set, to get help, is always welcome.

hidden_nurse_d5_3_f.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_3_f.text: *She opens the white plastic box at the side of the desk and takes out one first-aid information card.*

hidden_nurse_d5_4.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_4.text: During the festival, the emergency first-aid kit is by the gym's main entrance. If anyone gets hurt, don't tough it out. Call the teacher in charge right away.

hidden_nurse_d5_4_c.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d5_4_c.text: *In the square box at the bottom of the confirmation, a blue-ink stamp comes down clear: “Counseling concluded, rebook if needed.”*

hidden_nurse_d5_4_d.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_4_d.text: There. That finishes the last confirmation step, too.

hidden_nurse_d5_5.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_5.text: {name}. On your way, want to take one of these first-aid information cards?

hidden_nurse_d5_choice.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d5_choice.text: *The stiff card lists the basic first-aid steps on the front, and the school's official counseling channels on the back.*
choices: Yes. I'll keep it in my bag.
I'd rather know how to book the counseling center.
With this card, I won't need to go all the way to the counseling office.

hidden_nurse_d5_choice_a.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d5_choice_a.text: I'll keep it safe. If I don't get hurt, I can just leave it in the inside pocket of my bag, right? *She slides the card into a thin clear case and sets it on my palm.*

hidden_nurse_d5_choice_a_b.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_choice_a_b.text: Right. Best if you never have to take it out. But if your breath catches, or the moment comes when you need it, don't hesitate. Take it out right away.

hidden_nurse_d5_choice_b.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_choice_b.text: Good question. If you book ahead in the school app, even if I can't see you right away because I'm treating someone, a specialist counselor can take over at once.

hidden_nurse_d5_choice_b_b.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_choice_b_b.text: *With her index finger, she points to the small QR code printed in the corner on the back of the card.*

hidden_nurse_d5_choice_b_c.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_choice_b_c.text: Scan this, and the school app opens straight to the counseling booking window. Pick whichever is easier for you, the nurse's office or the school counseling center.

hidden_nurse_d5_choice_b_d.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_choice_b_d.text: Even when I'm away from my desk, another teacher will look after you and won't let it slip. Every record stays protected under school rules.

hidden_nurse_d5_choice_b_e.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d5_choice_b_e.text: *Along the bottom of the card, instead of a personal contact, the days and hours counseling is open, and the number for the department in charge, are printed neatly.*

hidden_nurse_d5_choice_b_f.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_choice_b_f.text: If something urgent comes up that you can't handle right away, who would you tell first?

hidden_nurse_d5_choice_b_g.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d5_choice_b_g.text: A guardian at home, or a teacher at school I'm close to. I won't swallow it and endure it alone the way I used to.

hidden_nurse_d5_6.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_6.text: *Only then do her eyes soften, as if she is relieved.* Do it that way, and that's enough. Here, the first-aid card.

hidden_nurse_d5_6_c.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d5_6_c.text: *At the very bottom of the card, a line in small sans-serif type catches my eye. “Reach out before the wound gets deeper.”*

hidden_nurse_d5_freetalk.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_freetalk.text: *She slides the finished counseling record into a file in the cabinet.* Official counseling ends here. Next time something hurts, don't hold it in. Tell me right away.

morning5_end.name: {name}
morning5_end.text: *I carefully sort the notes on the desk and gather them, then check every notification on my phone, one by one. My heart starts beating a little faster.*

morning5_committed_end.name: {name}
morning5_committed_end.text: *After I clear the desk, I fix the festival timetable in front of me once more, lined up with the route of the person I've already turned toward.*

hidden_nurse_d5_choice_trap.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_choice_trap.text: *She shakes her head firmly.* It's the opposite. This card isn't a charm to make you endure everything alone.

morning5_after_counteroffer.name: {name}
morning5_after_counteroffer.text: *A morning homeroom handout on the corner of the teacher's desk is pushed by the wind and slides to the floor without a sound. While no one readily bends to pick it up, the brisk broadcast opening the festival fills the classroom, gone cold.*

morning5_sojeong_1.name: {name}
morning5_sojeong_1.text: *I stand by the window and open the notes app. The cursor blinks in the thirty-ninth draft, erased and rewritten: the words I swallowed when I tried to report what Sojeong was going through.*

morning5_sojeong_2.name: {name}
morning5_sojeong_2.text: *I decide not to write a fortieth draft to defend myself. I copy the apology I put off for so long straight into the message box, and press send with a shaking thumb.*

morning5_sojeong_3.name: {name}
morning5_sojeong_3.text: I saw the graffiti on your desk back then, but I couldn't tell a teacher. Turning away and pretending not to know was my choice too. I'm truly sorry. You don't have to reply.

morning5_sojeong_4.name: {name}
morning5_sojeong_4.text: *A small sent mark appears beside the bubble. Instead of waiting on edge for the 1 to disappear, I calmly cover the screen and leave the chat.*

morning5_sojeong_5.name: {name}
morning5_sojeong_5.text: I would like formal counseling about something I looked past at the school before I transferred. *I send a message to my current homeroom teacher as well. I do not delete the two lines of confession I finally sent.*

morning5_caught_fallout_1.name: {name}
morning5_caught_fallout_1.text: *With the festival about to open, the classroom air is cold as ice. The three sit far apart, one in each corner, and the duty sheet on the board lists only dry, clerical assignments.*

morning5_caught_fallout_2.name: {name}
morning5_caught_fallout_2.text: *Yuna leaves first through the back door with the guidebooks. Dain walks toward the front door with a set face. Even Seoyeon, sorting the attendance sheet, never turns her head my way.*

morning5_caught_fallout_3.name: {name}
morning5_caught_fallout_3.text: *All through the morning event, the only thing that passed was the work that had to be checked. The moment their turns ended, the three split down different stairs, as if they had agreed.*

morning5_harem_fallout_1.name: {name}
morning5_harem_fallout_1.text: *The group chat only posts stiff notices for each time slot of the event. The three private chats that stayed lit for four days are all quiet, as if that were a lie.*

morning5_harem_fallout_2.name: Dain
morning5_harem_fallout_2.text: *Passing a corner in the hall, Dain pins it down in a low voice, her face set.* Even after today's event is over, don't call just one of us out alone. The three of us set that line. You keep it too.

morning5_harem_fallout_3.name: {name}
morning5_harem_fallout_3.text: *My lips move, then I nod without any strength. I watch for a long time as the three leave the school gate shoulder to shoulder, then follow behind them alone, a shadow one step late.*

morning5_counteroffer_choice.name: {name}
morning5_counteroffer_choice.text: *When the explanation that choked the room is over, both of them wait for the last answer, eyes fixed on my mouth.*
choices: Answer the person I promised first
Choose the person from last night
Let both of them go

morning5_counteroffer_choice_lead.name: {name}
morning5_counteroffer_choice_lead.text: *I turn straight toward the person I promised first and bow my head.* I'll apologize first for the choice I made last night, when I wavered. I won't shamelessly grab you now and ask you to stay beside me.

morning5_counteroffer_choice_tempter.name: {name}
morning5_counteroffer_choice_tempter.text: *I look at the person I spent last night with, then bow deep to the person I promised first.* I won't hide, like a coward, who my heart has leaned toward. Holding both of you and hurting you ends here.

morning5_counteroffer_choice_neither.name: {name}
morning5_counteroffer_choice_neither.text: *From between the two of them, I slowly take one step back.* I already broke that trust. I don't have the right to choose either of you now. I won't hold on to both of you out of my own greed.

morning5_counteroffer_gather.name: {name}
morning5_counteroffer_gather.text: *I message the person who stayed with me last night and say to meet in the classroom this morning, and I ask the person I originally promised to spare a little time. Soon the two open the classroom door, come in, and stop side by side by the window.*

morning5_mood_neg.name: {name}
morning5_mood_neg.text: *The first week since I transferred draws to a heavy close. I can't bring myself to face the names on the lock screen, and I only pull the bag zipper all the way shut.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_neg.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_neg.text: *She puts the brown manuscript envelope deep in the desk drawer and turns the key.* Let's end personal counseling here. I'll pass on the rest of the festival schedule only as a notice to the whole class.

hidden_nurse_d5_neg.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_neg.text: *The school nurse snaps the chart shut and closes the appointment sheet.* This hour, I'll only do emergency care. If you need a personal talk, request it through the school's official channel. *I turn and go back to the classroom.*
